subject: Post-demo: Asterion Labs — integration & routing options
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@asterionlabs.com>, Platform Team <platform@asterionlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Asterion Labs — integration & routing options

Hi Maya / Platform team,

Thanks again for taking the walkthrough today — great conversation and lots of alignment on goals. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

Call recap (short):
- Main goal: in-product semantic search + contextual assistants for support workflows.
- Primary constraints: EU data residency for EU users, sub-150ms median token latency for synchronous UI calls, budget sensitivity for high-volume embedding jobs.
- Integration preference surfaced: server-side SDK + OIDC-backed auth if possible.

Technical checklist / asks (please confirm or edit):
1) SDK language(s): Node.js (13.x) + Python (3.10) — confirm which language your integration team will own.
2) Auth: you mentioned OIDC. We can support OIDC (OIDC token exchange + short-lived node credentials) or API keys for server services. Which do you prefer for initial rollout?
3) Data flows: embeddings pipeline will be asynchronous (batch), but UI text generation needs low-latency synchronous routing. Confirm approximate concurrency for UI (p95 requests/sec per region).
4) Region routing: we propose EU region for EU users (data residency) and US for NA. Any APAC considerations?

Proposed model routing policy (high level):
- Low-latency path: quantized small LLM (fast) with strict token limits for UI first-pass.
- Fallback: full-precision medium LLM for degraded quality if small model hits hallucination/rate limit.
- Embeddings: dedicated dedicated embedding pool (batched, lower cost per vector) with automatic retry for partial failures.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (checklist + SDK quickstart), draft routing-policy-draft.yaml (policy example), cost-estimate-rough.xlsx (ballpark).

Next steps (suggested):
- You confirm SDK language and auth approach by Wed 3/16.
- We schedule a short (30m) engineering sync with your platform team + our infra lead (Jonas) for Thurs 3/17 to walk routing policy & quantization tradeoffs.
- I'll produce a first-draft routing policy config (yaml) ahead of that meeting.

If that timeline looks good, I'll lock the calendar.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments referenced: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf, routing-policy-draft.yaml, cost-estimate-rough.xlsx
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@asterionlabs.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@asterionlabs.com>, Alex Kim <akim@cloudops.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Asterion Labs — integration & routing options

Thanks Ava — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) SDK language: Platform will own Python for the backend jobs (embeddings) and Node for the UI ingestion layer. We'll be ready to take the Node quickstart.
2) Auth: OIDC is preferred. We need token exchange + short-lived credentials pattern so we can enforce per-service scoping. Can your OIDC integration support our IdP (AuthPoint)?
3) Latency: our target for synchronous UI is 120ms median for generation-first pass; we can tolerate slightly higher tail if we cache prefix responses client-side for repeated prompts.
4) Volume: expected embedding batch jobs ~200k vectors/month to start; query QPS for UI ~15-25 p95 across NA and EU (split ~55% NA / 45% EU).
5) Data residency: EU users must not leave EU region. We will need audit logs for all EU requests.

Two asks:
- Can you provide an example fallback chain that prioritizes latency but spills to higher-cost models when quality checks fail?
- Rough monthly cost range for the projected traffic (ballpark) — that will feed into our procurement discussion.

I'll confirm a room/time for Thurs but platform asked for a 45m slot to allow time for architecture detail.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform, Asterion Labs
maya.patel@asterionlabs.com | +44 20 7946 0123
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@asterionlabs.com>, Platform Team <platform@asterionlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Asterion Labs — integration & routing options

Maya — thanks for the detail. Quick answers and an attached working draft for the routing policy.

Auth / IdP: we support OIDC token exchange patterns and have customers on AuthPoint. Jonas will lead the integration work. We use short-lived tokens (5–15m) plus a service-side refresh for long-running jobs.

Routing / fallback (concrete example):
- Step 1 (UI fast-path): route to quantized low-latency model (redwood-small-quant) in the user region. Metrics: target median latency < 120ms, token limit 256.
- Step 2 (quality check): server-side filter validates output confidence score + reranker; if confidence < threshold or reranker score drops, call medium model (redwood-medium) in same region.
- Step 3 (degraded scenarios): if regional capacity constrained, failover to cross-region (US -> EU or EU -> US) based on policy + data residency guardrails (EU user data must not be served from US — we'll route to EU fallback pool only).
- Embeddings: batched embedding pool (autoscaled), retries with exponential backoff for partial failures, eventual-dead-letter for failed vectors to be manually re-ingested.

Cost control levers we recommend:
- Set per-route budget caps (tokens/minute) with soft alerts.
- Use dedicated quantized pools for UI-heavy routes.
- Schedule large embedding jobs in off-peak windows for cheaper throughput.

I've attached routing-policy-draft.yaml which includes the above and sample rules for: region_map, fallback_chain, confidence_thresholds, and token_caps. Also attached is cost-estimate-rough.xlsx with three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive).

Proposed next meeting: Thu 17 Mar 2027 11:00–11:45 PT — engineering sync with Jonas and our infra engagement. Please confirm availability.

I can also put together a quick SDK snippet showing OIDC token exchange and preferred header patterns if that would help Platform.

Cheers,
Ava
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: routing-policy-draft.yaml, cost-estimate-rough.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@asterionlabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Platform Team <platform@asterionlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Asterion Labs — integration & routing options

Thanks — I'll take point on the OIDC exchange flow and routing config. A couple quick clarifications before the sync: 

- KV cache TTL: for the UI fast-path we usually recommend 30–90s depending on prompt entropy. Do you want aggressive caching for repeated prompts (shorter TTL) or session affinity (longer TTL)?
- Embedding vector retention: what is the expected retention SLA (30/90/365 days)? That affects storage tiering and cost.

I will prepare a draft of the redwood deployment manifest and a sample routing-policy override that fits your EU residency rule (explicit region tags and audit-log forwarders). Bringing in Sean for cost-control knobs and SLA language.

Jonas Weber
Infra Eng Lead | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
